sentences.text: On August 25, 2023, a majority of a three-judge Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in part and reversed in part the district court's dismissal of the case, with a third judge dissenting on the basis that the district court did not err in dismissing the case.

On November 21, 2023, NVIDIA filed a motion with the Ninth Circuit for a stay of the mandate pending NVIDIA's petition for a writ of certiorari in the Supreme Court of the United States and the Supreme Court's resolution of the matter.
On October 8, 2021, the plaintiffs filed their Second Amended Consolidated Complaint based on the same alleged disclosure deficiencies.
The parties have agreed to settlement terms pending approval by the California Court.

comparisons.peer_topic: Securities class action lawsuit regarding segment reporting and foundry model
comparisons.peer_summary: A securities class action lawsuit was filed in May 2024 following the modification of segment reporting in Q1 2024 to align with the new internal foundry operating model; the case was consolidated in August 2024, with an amended complaint alleging violations of federal securities laws regarding the foundry business's growth prospects, and a motion to dismiss was filed in December 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and INTC disclose the status of securities class action lawsuits where the claims survived initial judicial scrutiny, moving the cases closer to potential resolution or further proceedings. NVDA's case was partially reinstated by the Ninth Circuit and is stayed pending certiorari. INTC's case was consolidated and an amended complaint was filed alleging false statements about the foundry business, with defendants filing a motion to dismiss. In both instances, the companies are actively defending against allegations that their public statements violated federal securities laws, unlike generic boilerplate disclosures.

sentences.text: On August 25, 2023, a majority of a three-judge Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in part and reversed in part the district court's dismissal of the case, with a third judge dissenting on the basis that the district court did not err in dismissing the case.
On December 5, 2023, the Ninth Circuit granted NVIDIA's motion to stay the mandate.

In August 2024 the court ordered the case consolidated with a second, similar lawsuit, and in October 2024 plaintiffs filed an amended consolidated complaint generally alleging that defendants violated the federal securities laws by making false or misleading statements about the growth and prospects of the foundry business and seeking monetary damages on behalf of all persons and entities that purchased or otherwise acquired our common stock or purchased call options or sold put options on our common stock from January 25, 2024 through August 1, 2024.
We filed a motion to dismiss the amended consolidated complaint in December 2024.
